questions.question: A researcher conducts a hypothesis test of $H_0: \mu = 100$ versus $H_a: \mu > 100$ at a significance level of $\alpha = 0.05$. Assuming the true population mean is actually $\mu = 108$, which of the following changes will increase the statistical power of the test?
options: Decreasing the population standard deviation $\sigma$ through improved measurement precision
Changing the alternative hypothesis to a two-sided test $H_a: \mu \neq 100$

questions.question: In a simple linear regression analysis predicting exam scores ($Y$) from study hours ($X$), the coefficient of determination is calculated as $R^2 = 0.64$. If the estimated slope of the regression line is negative, what is the sample correlation coefficient $r$ between study hours and exam scores?

A random sample of size $n = 64$ is drawn from a population with mean $\mu = 50$ and standard deviation $\sigma = 16$. According to the Central Limit Theorem, what is the approximate probability that the sample mean $\bar{X}$ exceeds $53$?

When performing an independent two-sample $t$-test to compare two population means ($H_0: \mu_1 - \mu_2 = 0$), under which of the following conditions is it appropriate to use a pooled two-sample $t$-test rather than Welch's $t$-test?
options: When the sample sizes $n_1$ and $n_2$ are extremely small ($n < 5$)
When the underlying population distributions are strongly skewed
When the explanatory variable has three or more categorical levels
When it is reasonable to assume that the two population variances are equal

questions.question: Calls arrive at a customer service helpdesk according to a Poisson process at an average rate of 4 calls per hour. What is the probability that the helpdesk receives exactly 2 calls in a given 30-minute interval?
